description: Every class and method of the scripting API, a line each (also: redgem api).
about: The scripting API of RedGem games: the classes and methods scripts use. Generated from docs/scripting/api.json, which tests keep in step with the engine.
notes: Script errors are logged with a backtrace and only disable the failing behaviour; the game keeps running. Every method takes finite numbers a float can hold: infinity, NaN or a number too large raises an `ArgumentError` instead of reaching the scene. A setting with a range raises outside it and says the range; nothing is quietly clamped, except `Vehicle#drive`'s inputs. Assigning `transform.position` to a physics object teleports it (moving bodies also stop); changing its rotation keeps its velocity. Images may be PNG, JPEG or static WebP (a name without an extension looks for `.webp` last), at most 8192 pixels a side; animated WebP and KTX2/Basis are not read. Missing or unreadable images (scene textures, `UI.image`, particle images) show an opaque magenta-and-black checkerboard, with a warning; a material that never named a texture keeps its plain color, and no path reads outside the game's folder.

classes.name: Vector3
classes.about: A point or a direction in meters: x, y, z.

methods.name: blender
methods.about: a vector given in Blender's axes (Z up)
whether the numbers are exactly the same

methods.name: clamped
methods.about: the same direction, no longer than max_length

methods.name: lerp
methods.about: the point t of the way to other

methods.name: with
methods.about: a copy with some parts changed: v.with(y: 0)

methods.name: approx?
methods.about: whether two vectors are about the same

classes.notes: `==` compares the numbers exactly, and equal vectors are one key of a `Hash`. A vector used as a key must not be changed in place (`set`, `add!`...) while the `Hash` holds it: use a `dup` as the key. The scene keeps positions, rotations and scales in 32-bit floats, so a vector that goes through it comes back rounded: compare what comes back from the scene with `approx?(other, tolerance)`. The in-place methods change the vector and hand it back: `dup` one you got from someone else first. Arithmetic whose result would not fit a float, and dividing by zero, raise an `ArgumentError`; a vector changed in place is then left as it was.

classes.notes: Every action, axis, binding and gamepad call takes `pad:` (0 to 3: the player; 0 when left out). Actions and axes come from `game.json`'s `input` section and `define_action`/`define_axis`; a player's bindings are kept between runs, beside the game's save. See [Controls](gameplay.md#controls).

classes.name: Audio
classes.about: Sounds and music from the game's sounds/ folder.

methods.name: play_at
methods.args: name, position, loop: false, volume: 1.0, pitch: 1.0, reference_distance: 1.0, max_distance: 50.0
methods.about: plays a sound at a place in the world; returns its id, or nil

methods.name: listener
methods.about: where the ears are (move it with the camera)

methods.name: move
methods.about: moves a sound played with play_at

methods.name: stop_sources
methods.about: stops every sound played with play_at

classes.notes: `play_at` sources use stereo panning and inverse-distance volume, fading to silence at `max_distance`. `volume` must be 0 or more and `pitch` from 0.01 to 8; `0 < reference_distance < max_distance`. Positions and directions may be arrays or `Vector3`. Update `Audio.listener(position, forward, up)` when the camera moves: nothing follows an object by itself. At most 64 sources play at once; old ids are never reused.

methods.about: draws the next texts with fonts/<name>.ttf or .otf (nil: the built-in face)

classes.notes: A focused widget (`focused: true`) is worked by Enter or a gamepad's A, and left and right change it. The built-in face adds glyphs as they are asked for (Greek, Cyrillic, accented letters, `€`); for another face or script, put a `.ttf` or `.otf` in `fonts/` and set `UI.font`. A missing or unreadable face falls back to the built-in one, with a warning; glyphs a face lacks show as `?`; there is no bidirectional layout or complex-script shaping.
